notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none; the card's RosDriver helper and cap.sensing.image.v1 class express the actual ROS 2 runtime. The pinned node is a Python ROS 2 node over rosbridge, so no Python native class is declared and no native.py exists. Scope: the fixed sensor_msgs/msg/CompressedImage JPEG stream on the relative 'raspicam_compressed' topic (resolved '/raspicam/raspicam_compressed' under the constructor's 'raspicam' namespace) is the primary and only working image path. The uncompressed branch at ros2_raspicam_node.py:93 references the unimported name Image, so it is not exposed. No CameraInfo stream exists. Camera settings are ROS parameters read once at construction; this package invents no parameter service and exposes no metadata-only substitute. No stop or safe-state binding is declared: the pinned node exposes no ROS service or action that stops capture, destroy_node only closes the camera on node destruction, and closing a subscription would not stop physical acquisition. The fake is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport that answers the declared subscription and returns a 2x2 placeholder JPEG, marked as placeholder in fake.py; it is not a replay of captured ROS traffic and claims F0 contract evidence only. The SDK's single fixed image subscription returns decoded pixels and dimensions; it does not attach the upstream header, and the upstream node itself only sets frame_id to a frame number and leaves the stamp at its default. Real deployment image size is whatever camera_image_width/camera_image_height select (their 640/480 values are parameter defaults, not device bounds); the default local artifact store caps one image at 2 MiB, larger decoded PNGs need a programmatic store with a higher max_artifact_bytes (absolute 16 MiB), and max_input_bytes, max_pixels, timeout_ms and max_message_bytes are client execution bounds, not camera limits. The fake returns a smaller image than a real deployment; the real size is configuration-dependent and no source states a universal bound. Deployment still requires ROS 2, python3-picamera and a Raspberry Pi camera on the pinned legacy platform (README.md:18-29); the card's install block is empty and no install or live ROS run was performed. The hardware backend was never started; RosDriver refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review, and driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null with a model authored_by. Fake gate evidence is contract_checked only; it does not establish a real ROS graph, camera, latency or hardware run. G8 passed with the expected G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warning because the driver has no actuating numeric limit to probe.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the R0 camera contract against the pinned node, as the triage predicted after the capability-class override: the relative topic raspicam_compressed under namespace raspicam resolves to /raspicam/raspicam_compressed (ros2_raspicam_node.py:30, 33-35, 88-91; README.md:7), the CompressedImage type (:23), the fake's ROS 2 header (stamp left 0 because the node never sets it, :187), every fact and the bounded capture. One fact said more than its lines ('no ROS service or action calls it' for destroy_node, 80-86); the reviewer narrowed it and added three source facts (main calls stop_workers and destroy_node only after spin, 252-266; the only stamp assignment is commented out, 180-187; the node's own has_parameter helper calls get_parameter and reads NOT_SET as unset, 229-249) in driver.py and facts.md (with a start-up note), and regenerated reference.json and REFERENCE.md; the gate and collect.py --strict pass, digest unchanged (sha256:62b0b8955782579bfa143edebd8f3295a16ce2d14f9fca01cde0448323513e6d). For the human reviewer: Passive camera; the RosDriver only subscribes to a running graph. Start-up of this 2018 node on a current ROS 2 is not established: it overrides has_parameter with a helper that calls get_parameter and expects NOT_SET for undeclared names (229-249), which rclpy releases that declare parameters before reading them may refuse (rclpy is outside the clone; not run). A node that does not start shows as capture timeouts, never as an image. It needs python3-picamera, the legacy Raspberry Pi camera stack.
